proposal_scope: Unregistered invented kernel:22working units are partitioned into11plain and11accented forms, paired by11base identities. Atmostone accented occurrence per complete written word; one written group is one word. No actual pairing, source alphabet, accent meaning, code table, source corpus or complete historical writer chosen.
proof: Any two DISTINCT accented forms must never cooccur in a complete written group. Repeated occurrences of the same accent are also prohibited by the draft, but not needed for this necessary obstruction.
Eleven distinct accent forms require C(11,2)=55 absent unordered distinct-unit pairs. Any bijective renaming preserves this count.
The fixed22-unit universe has C(22,2)=231pairs. Old1296reports218/220/218cooccurring pairs, leaving13/11/13absent pairs. Each is less than55, so no proposed11-unit accent class is possible.

More generally the aggregate absence counts alone bound such a class to atmost5units: C(5,2)=10 while C(6,2)=15. This is only an upper bound, not existence of a5-unit class; do not automatically select that smaller alternative.
decision: Do not implement this eleven-base/single-accent kernel or register it as an unexecuted promising candidate. No newly fitted alphabet or source assumptions. No smaller accent class or extraaccent exception selected after this result.
limits: Conditional exact22unit andcomplete-group panel, allrare forms retained; no new physicalglyph validation.
Different readers are alternate readings of one manuscript.
Not general vowel/stress/phonology rejection, and not a complete writer refutation: no complete writer was specified.
The old1296LOW_ACTIVITY decision with its5percent gate remains unchanged. This arithmetic uses only its published pair counts, not that gate.
No new manuscript data, nativeword meaning, image, source corpus, rawTSV, reserve or sealed material.
